<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation
SGLang HiCache stores one logical page as several per-pool Mooncake objects, keyed as `{key_prefix}_{page_hash}{suffix}`. An external KV-aware router that wants to score L3 hits must rebuild exactly these keys, but the suffix depends on the model's pool layout, the parallelism layout, and the resolved `--page-size`, so deriving it outside the engine is fragile and breaks silently whenever the naming changes. Mooncake already models per-pool hit policies internally (`PoolHitPolicy`: ALL_PAGES / TRAILING_PAGES); this PR surfaces the same information to external consumers.

This is the engine-side producer for the Dynamo KV router change (ai-dynamo/dynamo#14720), which consumes this layout to reconstruct the object keys.

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->

## Modifications

- New engine endpoint `GET /get_hicache_l3_cache_layout`, following the existing `GetInternalStateReq` tokenizer→scheduler round-trip. Returns the per-pool layout: key suffixes, hit policy, trailing-page window, the key prefix, and the rank that produced it. Returns `"enabled": false` (with a debug log naming the reason) when hierarchical caching is disabled or the L3 backend is not Mooncake.
- The layout is assembled by `MooncakeStore.describe_l3_object_layout`, which reuses `_get_hybrid_page_component_keys` — the same key-building code the store writes objects with — so the reported naming cannot drift from the stored keys.
- CPU-only unit tests in `test/registered/hicache/test_hicache_l3_object_layout.py` (registered under `base-a-test-cpu`), and a section in `docs/docs/advanced_features/hicache_design.mdx`.

Two scoping decisions, happy to revisit:
- The endpoint mirrors `/model_info` (no auth); can add `AuthLevel.ADMIN_OPTIONAL` to match the adjacent `/hicache/storage-backend` if preferred.
- Suffixes are rank-independent for single-PP MLA models; with `pp_size > 1` or an MHA layout they embed the rank. The response reports `pp_rank`/`pp_size` so a consumer can check whether one response covers the whole deployment.


<!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. -->

## Accuracy Tests
N/A — introspection-only change; does not affect model outputs.
<!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. -->

## Speed Tests and Profiling



N/A — the endpoint is queried out-of-band by an external router and touches no inference path.


<!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. -->

## Checklist

- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

sure, I'd like to add it to the existing GetServerInfo.json_info — same path kv-events discovery already uses

Three correctness issues are detailed inline. Validation used dependency-isolated, method-level reproductions of the current source; the missing import is also reported by the lint run for this head. Full runtime and GPU end-to-end tests were not run.

[P1] Import `msgspec_to_builtins` before invoking this handler

`msgspec_to_builtins` is neither imported nor defined in this module, so every call to `/get_hicache_l3_cache_layout` raises `NameError`, including when HiCache is disabled. `process_input_requests()` does not catch this exception; it propagates to `run_scheduler_process()`, whose exception handler sends `SIGQUIT` to the parent process. A metadata query can therefore terminate the service.

A method-level invocation reproduces the `NameError`, and [the lint run for this head](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/38153300828) reports the same F821 error. Please import the helper from `sglang.srt.utils.msgspec_utils` and add a test that actually invokes the scheduler handler.

nodes.body:
[P2] Include the primary storage pools in the advertised layout

`sidecar_pool_specs` excludes the primary KV, SWA, and Mamba pools, even though those pools can be required to restore a prefix. Consequently, a plain KV model returns an empty `pools` list, and a DeepSeek V4 layout omits the required SWA objects.

In a method-level reproduction with a logical KV anchor, C4/C4-state sidecars, and SWA, all advertised sidecar objects exist but the SWA objects are missing. Checking only the advertised keys reports a hit, while the original `batch_exists_v2()` returns zero restorable pages. An external router can therefore overestimate reusable KV.

Please describe all physical pools required by storage prefetch, including the physical KV anchor and component-owned pools, with their actual hit policies and trailing windows. Logical anchors that have no stored object should remain excluded.

nodes.body:
[P2] Forward the layout through the DP controller startup handshake

When `num_dp_ranks > 1`, the engine receives its startup information from `DataParallelController`. `launch_tensor_parallel_group()` only retains selected fields from the scheduler replies, and `run_data_parallel_controller_process()` constructs a new `init_info` dictionary without `hicache_object_layout`. The field added here is therefore discarded before it reaches the HTTP/gRPC frontend, so `/server_info` and `GetServerInfo.json_info` omit the advertised layout in DP deployments.

Executing the existing aggregation statements with a scheduler reply containing this field reproduces the loss. Please retain and forward the layout through the DP controller, and add a test covering that handshake; the new server-info tests inject a prebuilt `scheduler_info` and therefore bypass this path.

files.patch:
@@ -174,6 +174,12 @@ HiCache encapsulates all read, write, and query operations on L3 backends within
 
 Specifically, **LMCache**, an efficient KV cache layer for enterprise-scale LLM inference, provides an alternative solution to HiCache. Try LMCache [here](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/tree/main/python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/storage/lmcache).
 
+### External KV Router Integration
+
+HiCache is not only consumed inside SGLang. An external KV-aware router placed in front of the engines can also query the same L3 data to route requests to the instance that can reuse the most KV cache. Such a router must rebuild the exact object keys the backend uses, which for Mooncake is `{key_prefix}_{page_hash}{suffix}`. The suffix depends on the model's pool layout, the parallelism layout, and the resolved `--page-size`, so the engine exposes its layout instead of letting each router derive the naming itself.
+
+For this purpose the Mooncake backend reports the layout of every registered pool: the key suffixes, the hit policy, and, for pools that only cover a trailing window of pages (the sliding-window states), the window size. A router that requires every pool on every page scores sequences with sliding-window states as misses, so the hit policy distinguishes the two cases. The suffixes are rank-independent for single-PP MLA models; with `pp_size > 1` or an MHA layout they embed the rank, so the layout also reports which rank produced it. When hierarchical caching is disabled or the L3 backend is not Mooncake, the layout is reported as unavailable.
+
 ## Related Parameters
 
 - **`--enable-hierarchical-cache`**: Enable hierarchical cache functionality. This is required to use HiCache.

+"""
+Unit tests for the HiCache L3 (mooncake) object-key layout reported to external
+KV routers via GET /get_hicache_l3_cache_layout.
+
+python3 -m unittest hicache.test_hicache_l3_object_layout.TestHiCacheL3ObjectLayout
+"""
+
+import unittest
+
+from sglang.srt.mem_cache.hicache_storage import (
+    PoolHitPolicy,
+    PoolName,
+    SidecarPoolSpec,
+)
+from sglang.srt.mem_cache.storage.mooncake_store.mooncake_store import MooncakeStore
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
+
+register_cpu_ci(est_time=5, suite="base-a-test-cpu")
+
+
+def _sidecar(pool_name: PoolName, hit_policy: PoolHitPolicy) -> SidecarPoolSpec:
+    indices_from_pool = (
+        PoolName.SWA if hit_policy is PoolHitPolicy.TRAILING_PAGES else PoolName.KV
+    )
+    return SidecarPoolSpec(
+        pool_name=pool_name,
+        indices_from_pool=indices_from_pool,
+        hit_policy=hit_policy,
+    )
+
+
+class TestHiCacheL3ObjectLayout(CustomTestCase):
+    def _store(self, *, mla_suffix="", pp_rank=0, pp_size=1, registered=()):
+        store = MooncakeStore.__new__(MooncakeStore)
+        # A real store needs a live mooncake master; the host pools are
+        # sentinels because the DeepSeek V4 branch only checks registration.
+        store.registered_pools = {name: object() for name in registered}
+        store.mla_suffix = mla_suffix
+        store.mha_suffix = "0"
+        store.is_mla_backend = True
+        store.pp_rank = pp_rank
+        store.pp_size = pp_size
+        store.config_prefix = "tag_my-model"
+        return store
+
+    def test_layout_reports_suffixes_prefix_and_hit_policy(self):
+        store = self._store(
+            registered=(PoolName.DEEPSEEK_V4_C4, PoolName.DEEPSEEK_V4_C4_STATE)
+        )
+
+        layout = store.describe_l3_object_layout(
+            sidecar_pool_specs=[
+                _sidecar(PoolName.DEEPSEEK_V4_C4, PoolHitPolicy.ALL_PAGES),
+                _sidecar(PoolName.DEEPSEEK_V4_C4_STATE, PoolHitPolicy.TRAILING_PAGES),
+            ],
+            swa_trailing_pages=2,
+            page_size=64,
+        )
+
+        self.assertEqual(layout["backend"], "mooncake")
+        self.assertEqual(layout["page_size"], 64)
+
+        object_layout = layout["hicache_object_layout"]
+        self.assertEqual(object_layout["key_prefix"], "tag_my-model")
+        self.assertTrue(object_layout["is_mla_backend"])
+        self.assertEqual(object_layout["pp_rank"], 0)
+        self.assertEqual(object_layout["pp_size"], 1)
+        self.assertEqual(
+            object_layout["pools"],
+            [
+                {
+                    "pool": "deepseek_v4_c4",
+                    "suffixes": ["__deepseek_v4_c4"],
+                    "hit_policy": "all_pages",
+                },
+                {
+                    "pool": "deepseek_v4_c4_state",
+                    "suffixes": ["__deepseek_v4_c4_state"],
+                    "hit_policy": "trailing_pages",
+                    "trailing_pages": 2,
+                },
+            ],
+        )
+
+    def test_layout_skips_pools_that_are_not_registered(self):
+        store = self._store(registered=(PoolName.DEEPSEEK_V4_C4,))
+
+        layout = store.describe_l3_object_layout(
+            sidecar_pool_specs=[
+                _sidecar(PoolName.DEEPSEEK_V4_C4, PoolHitPolicy.ALL_PAGES),
+                _sidecar(PoolName.DEEPSEEK_V4_C128, PoolHitPolicy.ALL_PAGES),
+            ],
+            swa_trailing_pages=None,
+            page_size=64,
+        )
+
+        pools = layout["hicache_object_layout"]["pools"]
+        self.assertEqual([entry["pool"] for entry in pools], ["deepseek_v4_c4"])
+
+    def test_layout_suffixes_embed_the_pp_rank(self):
+        store = self._store(
+            mla_suffix="1",
+            pp_rank=1,
+            pp_size=2,
+            registered=(PoolName.DEEPSEEK_V4_C4,),
+        )
+
+        layout = store.describe_l3_object_layout(
+            sidecar_pool_specs=[
+                _sidecar(PoolName.DEEPSEEK_V4_C4, PoolHitPolicy.ALL_PAGES)
+            ],
+            swa_trailing_pages=None,
+            page_size=64,
+        )
+
+        object_layout = layout["hicache_object_layout"]
+        self.assertEqual(object_layout["pools"][0]["suffixes"], ["_1_deepseek_v4_c4"])
+        self.assertEqual(object_layout["pp_rank"], 1)
+        self.assertEqual(object_layout["pp_size"], 2)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()

inline_comments.body:
[P1] Import `msgspec_to_builtins` before invoking this handler

`msgspec_to_builtins` is neither imported nor defined in this module, so every call to `/get_hicache_l3_cache_layout` raises `NameError`, including when HiCache is disabled. `process_input_requests()` does not catch this exception; it propagates to `run_scheduler_process()`, whose exception handler sends `SIGQUIT` to the parent process. A metadata query can therefore terminate the service.

A method-level invocation reproduces the `NameError`, and [the lint run for this head](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/38153300828) reports the same F821 error. Please import the helper from `sglang.srt.utils.msgspec_utils` and add a test that actually invokes the scheduler handler.

inline_comments.body:
[P2] Include the primary storage pools in the advertised layout

`sidecar_pool_specs` excludes the primary KV, SWA, and Mamba pools, even though those pools can be required to restore a prefix. Consequently, a plain KV model returns an empty `pools` list, and a DeepSeek V4 layout omits the required SWA objects.

In a method-level reproduction with a logical KV anchor, C4/C4-state sidecars, and SWA, all advertised sidecar objects exist but the SWA objects are missing. Checking only the advertised keys reports a hit, while the original `batch_exists_v2()` returns zero restorable pages. An external router can therefore overestimate reusable KV.

Please describe all physical pools required by storage prefetch, including the physical KV anchor and component-owned pools, with their actual hit policies and trailing windows. Logical anchors that have no stored object should remain excluded.

inline_comments.body:
[P2] Forward the layout through the DP controller startup handshake

When `num_dp_ranks > 1`, the engine receives its startup information from `DataParallelController`. `launch_tensor_parallel_group()` only retains selected fields from the scheduler replies, and `run_data_parallel_controller_process()` constructs a new `init_info` dictionary without `hicache_object_layout`. The field added here is therefore discarded before it reaches the HTTP/gRPC frontend, so `/server_info` and `GetServerInfo.json_info` omit the advertised layout in DP deployments.

Executing the existing aggregation statements with a scheduler reply containing this field reproduces the loss. Please retain and forward the layout through the DP controller, and add a test covering that handshake; the new server-info tests inject a prebuilt `scheduler_info` and therefore bypass this path.
